headline: Costs will rise next year for NC state employees and teachers who use most WakeMed services
summary: The North Carolina State Health Plan aims to lower costs by implementing a new provider ranking system. WakeMed will become non-preferred, increasing out-of-pocket costs for members using State Health Plan, while Duke Health will remain access providers. UNC Health is preferred, potentially reducing costs for users.

headline: Lee County residents demand pause on NC data center, claiming deception
summary: Residents protest proposed data center in Lee County due to concerns about noise pollution and potential health impacts. Around 150 residents attended a Board of Commissioners meeting to voice their opposition.

headline: New poll shows Whatley within striking distance of Cooper as GOP support coalesces
summary: A PPP poll shows Gov. Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley by 4 points in the U.S. Senate race, but the race remains competitive and is likely to tighten come November.

headline: Oklahoma confirms spike in cases of cyclosporiasis as U.S. outbreak spreads
summary: Oklahoma reports 56 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases, with six hospitalizations. The CDC scaled back surveillance for foodborne illnesses like cyclospora in 2015. Public health recommendations include hand washing and avoiding raw foods to prevent infection.

headline: CDC nominee on shaky ground following US Senate confirmation hearing
summary: Dr. Erica Schwartz's nomination to lead the CDC faced resistance at a Senate confirmation hearing due to concerns about her independence from political influence and commitment to public health transparency. Democrats and key Republicans expressed skepticism, potentially jeopardizing her confirmation.

headline: Trump presses ICE to continue traffic stops despite fatal shootings
summary: President Trump ordered ICE officers to resume traffic stops, reversing a one-day pause following two fatal shootings of immigrants during such stops. The move sparked criticism from lawmakers and international leaders alike, calling for investigations and ICE reform.

headline: Candidates for the Kansas education board’s most rural district share their views on funding, DEI
summary: Three candidates for Kansas State Board of Education's District 5 differ on funding strategies and diversity initiatives. Jean Clifford, a former board member, backs increased special education funds but opposes DEI practices. Kelly Ancar, a nurse, favors accountability over additional funds and supports compliance with regulations. Lorie Wood, an educator, advocates for equitable resources in rural schools and inclusive programs.

headline: Kansas cyclospora cases more than double this week, as illness spreads nationally
summary: Kansas cases of cyclosporiasis doubled this week to 55, with national CDC reports showing over 7,000 cases. Lettuces and salad greens are likely sources, but no specific products have been identified. Proper produce handling and hygiene can reduce risk.

headline: Kansas health agency says Galena landfill fire is out, more work to be done
summary: The smoldering fire at Galena Landfill has been extinguished after excavation work by Jordan Disposal. Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) will monitor soil cover completion. Residents worry about air pollution data inconsistency, affecting their quality of life. KDHE's involvement indicates potential public health concerns.

headline: Hospital CEOs meet union skepticism over out-of-state acquisition of Allina Health
summary: Labor unions express concerns about the proposed merger of Allina Health and Sutter Health, fearing increased healthcare costs and decreased care quality. The Minnesota Attorney General's Office, now empowered to analyze and block hospital mergers, hosts public forums to gauge public interest. Unions demand a written 'community benefits agreement' to protect workers and patients. Public health implications are not directly discussed but the merger could impact access and affordability of healthcare services in Minnesota.

headline: ICE should continue traffic stops despite recent shootings, Trump says, seeming to oppose new suspension
summary: President Trump urged ICE to resume vehicle stops despite recent fatal shootings of immigrants during such operations.

headline: “ICE is everywhere”: In Houston, fear and grief permeate Latino neighborhoods after fatal shooting
summary: The shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by an ICE agent in Houston has caused fear among residents of Magnolia Park neighborhood, potentially impacting community trust in immigration enforcement agencies.

headline: TribCast: An ICE shooting roils Houston
summary: A community vigil was held for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who was fatally shot by an ICE officer in Houston.

headline: Texas agencies must cut spending by 3% under new order from Abbott, Patrick and Burrows
summary: Texas lawmakers signed into law a bill creating the Texas Department of Government Efficiency on April 23, 2025. This new department aims to improve state agency operations and reduce costs. The signing ceremony was attended by Governor Greg Abbott, House Speaker Dustin Burrows, and Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick. While the article does not explicitly mention the state budget, the creation of this department suggests an effort to identify potential savings or efficiencies that could impact future budget planning and allocations.

headline: Crowd packs Houston City Hall to demand action, express anger after ICE shooting
summary: Houston Mayor John Whitmire addressed citizens at a City Council meeting on July 14, following protests over the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by an immigration agent on July 7.

headline: Most NJ voters oppose movie theaters selling booze, poll says
summary: Most New Jersey voters oppose expanding liquor sales in movie theaters, according to a Fairleigh Dickinson University poll. The Assembly approved a bill creating a new type of liquor license for theaters, but it faces Senate opposition due to public skepticism about loosening alcohol regulations.

headline: Kansas City keeps approving subsidies without knowing whether they work
summary: The Kansas City Council lacks comprehensive data on economic development benefits despite approving over $1 billion in subsidies.

headline: Idaho U.S. Rep. Russ Fulcher seeks input on federal land management in survey
summary: Rep. Russ Fulcher launched a survey to gather Idahoans' views on federal lands management. A recent Boise State University poll found that 46.4% oppose transferring federal land management to the state due to potential taxpayer costs, while 35% support it.

headline: Morrisey’s review of TANF spending has forced some WV community and technical colleges to cut jobs
summary: Due to a $43M structural deficit in Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds, Governor Morrisey's review may impact student support programs at West Virginia colleges. Some coordinators helping students access essential resources have been temporarily cut due to delayed funding disbursement. The review could result in cuts to other TANF-supported programs like child care assistance. Lawmakers are frustrated by the lack of communication from the governor's office about these changes, which could impact budget allocations.

headline: Pillen memo calling for 5% cut across Nebraska agencies raises questions about governor’s authority
summary: Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen issued a memo calling for a minimum 5% spending cut across state agencies to address projected budget deficits of $172 million and $631 million for the current and next biennial budgets, respectively. Critics argue this oversteps his authority as he signed off on the budget already, but Pillen maintains it's a collaborative process aimed at balancing future budgets. The University of Nebraska is expected to cut around $36 million from its operating budget.

headline: Virginia among states hit by cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to fresh produce and more headlines
summary: Virginia experiencing cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to fresh produce.

headline: Ohio Republican attorney general candidate appears to advocate ending parts of Medicaid
summary: Ohio Auditor Keith Faber has suggested potentially ending some parts of Ohio Medicaid due to fraud concerns. Faber's comments come amidst federal discussions about funding cuts for Medicaid. No direct mention or impact on state budget was discussed in the article.

headline: 5th Circuit Court of Appeals reverses its decision, allowing ICE to hold detainees indefinitely
summary: The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a decision requiring ICE to provide bond hearings within 90 days for immigrants arrested within the country, indefinitely delaying release decisions for over 600 detainees in Mississippi.

headline: With SC spending plan at an impasse, legislators float not passing a new budget at all
summary: Legislators remain at an impasse over South Carolina's state budget two weeks into the fiscal year. Three options are on the table: cut $430 million in legislative pet projects and property tax breaks, meet in the middle, or pass no new budget, leaving funding at last year's levels. Failing to pass a budget could harm agencies like Medicaid and education, impacting services and raises for teachers and state employees.

headline: Hundreds protest outside Scarborough ICE facility after fatal Biddeford shooting
summary: Following the fatal shooting of Johan Sebastián by ICE agents in Biddeford, Maine, protests erupted across the state demanding changes to immigration enforcement policies. Hundreds gathered outside ICE facilities in Scarborough and Portland, calling for defunding and abolishing ICE. State lawmakers joined protesters, echoing demands for oversight and transparency, with the Maine Attorney General's Office investigating the incident. An armed counter-protester attempted to disrupt the rally at the Scarborough facility but was eventually led out.

headline: No immediate threat of New World screwworm affecting South Dakota, state vet says
summary: The USDA is monitoring New World screwworm cases in Texas and South Dakota is currently unaffected. South Dakota's veterinary inspection system helps prevent spread. State veterinarian Mendel Miller has no immediate concerns due to containment efforts in Texas, but notes climate change could shift infection boundaries northward. The USDA is using sterile flies for eradication efforts.

headline: Ferguson kicks off fight to defeat WA initiative to repeal income tax
summary: Governor Bob Ferguson, opposing Initiative 645 which seeks to repeal Washington's new high-earner income tax, kicked off a campaign to defeat it. The initiative has gathered over 500,000 signatures and awaits verification for ballot qualification. Opponents argue the tax ensures wealthier residents pay their fair share while helping lower-income residents through tax cuts and credits.
